items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: Bill Miller, Sinatra’s longtime accompanist, was on the podium conducting.

ctx.x: Yeah. It’s a matter of going in and playing the situation. I’m going to play pretty much – you know just basically when I’m playing for a singer I’m going to play less fills than – I’m going to play as few fills as I can to still do the right thing. I’m going to play – I’m going to voice my chords in such a way that I’m not colliding with their note. If she’s singing an A flat I’m not going to play an A flat flat nine with the A on top. The flat nine on top. I’m not going to push and lead the way. I think where…

the right register of the piano an in an intelligent way. I learned a lot about that from trial and error as a young accompanist in church. And then I learned watching and listening to Jimmy Rowles accompany singers and Mike Wofford and Bobby Tucker, and the list goes on. Great accompanists. I also learned a lot about accompanying singers by listening to the arrangements that Billy May and Heimey Bow and Gordon Jenkins and Nelson Riddle did for singers. When I worked the brief stint with Sinatra that I did, I was…
What is an annoyance to you in the music business? That’s a broad question but I’m thinking in trio settings? You seem like a fairly calm person to me. What gets under your skin?
